summary: OctoLong is a data pipeline that uses an AST parser, a Python language server (jedi) and the package manager inside a container to recursively pull in the implementations a Python file calls, including from installed third-party packages, yielding dependency-dense code contexts up to 128K+ tokens. The authors mix ~6.2B such tokens (~12%) into a ~50B-token context-extension corpus, mid-train Qwen3 0.6B-14B base models to 128K, then SFT on ~10B tokens, and compare against 18 open-weight long-context models plus three ablations on long-context code, general long-context, tool-use and short-context coding benchmarks.

claims.claim: Replacing conventional long-context data with OctoLong cross-repo code improves long-context code understanding.
claims.evidence: Table 3 ablation (8B only): '-Cross-Repo Code' is lower by 3.38 (LooGLE V2 Code), 2.84 (LongCodeQA), 3.05 (RepoQA). Single 8B run per variant, no seeds or CIs; ablation swaps in a ProLong-style control corpus whose composition (Table 2) differs in several categories, so the effect is not cleanly isolated to the 12% slice.

claims.claim: Gains transfer to downstream agentic tool use.
claims.evidence: Table 4: ablation drops 3.91 on BFCL V3 and 4.97 on tau2-Bench; OctoLong-14B 67.31 BFCL / 34.42 tau2 vs Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct-1M 55.59 / 26.02. No SWE-bench or repository-editing agent evaluation despite 'agentic workflows' framing; baselines are older-generation models with different post-training.

claims.claim: OctoLong preserves short-context coding and improves API usage.
claims.evidence: Table 4: OctoLong-8B is below official Qwen3-8B by 2.36 (LiveCodeBench V6) and 1.29 (BigCodeBench Hard); improvement is only vs its own ablations. 'No penalty' framing in §1 is overstated.

claims.claim: Despite Python-only data, benefits transfer to other programming languages.
claims.evidence: Inferred from RepoQA (five languages) averages; no per-language breakdown vs ablation in the main text.

patterns.note: Deterministic AST+LSP+package-manager traversal is the core retrieval mechanism for building dependency-dense context; evidence is via training gains, not inference-time retrieval.
Motivated by cross-repository dependencies (code not self-contained per repo), but only for training data, not for agent coordination across repos.
Mid-training/SFT data recipe with ablations improves tool-use benchmarks for small open models.

methodology.sample: 12K installable Python repos, 92K seed files; ~6.2B OctoLong tokens; evaluation on LooGLE V2 Code, LongCodeQA, RepoQA, LongBench V2, OpenAI MRCR, AA-LCR, BFCL V3, tau2-Bench, LiveCodeBench V6, BigCodeBench Hard.
methodology.baselines: 18 open-weight long-context LMs (e.g., Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct-1M, GLM-4-9B-1M, Yi-Coder-9B, Llama-3 variants, ProLong, UltraLong); no closed or latest-generation agentic models.
methodology.models: OctoLong-Instruct derived from Qwen3 dense base 0.6B-14B.
methodology.variance: Not reported; single training run per config, sampling at T=0.6 with no repeated-run statistics.
methodology.ablations: Three on 8B: minus cross-repo code, minus model merging, minus context extension.
methodology.contamination_controls: 13-gram decontamination against all downstream evals (App. B); LiveCodeBench restricted to V6 split.
methodology.languages: Python-only training contexts; RepoQA covers five languages.

standards.peer_review: arXiv preprint, no venue in comment or journal_ref.
standards.artifacts: No code, data or model release link found in the text.

biases.detail: Pipeline and all mined contexts are Python (jedi); cross-language transfer is asserted from one benchmark.
Ablation deltas of 2-5 points from single training runs.
No release of pipeline, OctoLong data, or OctoLong-Instruct checkpoints is stated.
'Virtually limitless source' and 'no penalty on short-context' while Table 4 shows Qwen3-8B ahead on short-context coding.
-Cross-Repo Code replaces OctoLong data with a ProLong control mix; Table 2 shows the two mixes differ across many categories, so the effect is not cleanly attributable to cross-repo code.

verdict_reason: Reasonably broad evaluation with ablations and decontamination, but single runs, an imperfectly isolated ablation, Python-only data, no artifact release, and it concerns model training rather than harness design.
applicability: Mostly does not transfer: the team will not mid-train models. The one transferable idea is harness-side: build cross-repo context by deterministic dependency traversal (AST + language server + build-tool metadata) rather than embedding search. For a Java team whose ingestion spans several repositories, the analogue is using jdtls/Maven or Gradle coordinates to resolve calls into sibling ingestion libraries and shared DTO/contract modules and feeding those to whichever agent host is in use. The paper gives no evidence for this at inference time or for Java, so treat it as a hypothesis to test, not a result.
